summary: Any adjacent price change can affect the maximum profit, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n prices in the worst case. The greedy scan processes each adjacent pair once.

optimality.argument: If an algorithm leaves some price unread, changing that value can create or remove a profitable adjacent rise while all inspected values remain fixed. Exact computation therefore requires Omega(n) price inspections in the worst case. The candidate evaluates each of the n - 1 adjacent differences once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unseen price can change one or two adjacent contributions and therefore change the optimum, so arbitrary input positions cannot be skipped.
The candidate performs constant work for each adjacent price pair.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover separated rises, one continuous rise, and no profitable rise; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
